{{Short description|French organic chemist}}
'''Pierre Sinaÿ''', born on April 11, 1938, in [[Aulnay-sous-Bois]] ([[Seine-et-Oise]]), is a French organic [[chemist]].

== Biography ==
After studying at the [[École nationale supérieure des industries chimiques|École nationale supérieure des industries chimiques de Nancy]] from 1958 to 1961, he obtained a doctorate under the supervision of Professor Serge David in 1966 and continued for two years at [[Harvard University]] in [[Massachusetts]] (United States) as a post-doctoral researcher with Professor Roger W. Jeanloz.<ref name="academie">{{Cite web|url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/membres/S/Sinay_Pierre_bio.htm|title=Biographie (Académie des sciences)|accessdate=Apr 24, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110113154959/http://www.academie-sciences.fr/membres/S/Sinay_Pierre_bio.htm|archive-date=January 13, 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> He then entered the [[University of Orléans]] in 1969 as a professor, where he was Director of the Institute of Organic and Analytical Chemistry from 1978 to 1987.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.icoa.fr/|title=Institute of Organic and Analytical Chemistry - ICOA UMR 7311 &#124; Institute of Organic and Analytical Chemistry - ICOA UMR 7311|website=www.icoa.fr|accessdate=Apr 24, 2020}}</ref> He then became Professor of Chemistry in 1986 at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University|Université Pierre-et-Marie-Curie]], where he then headed the Laboratory of Selective Processes in Organic and Bioorganic Chemistry in the Department of Chemistry at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]]. He then became Professor Emeritus at [[Sorbonne University]] in 2006 and joined the Paris Institute of Molecular Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ipcm.fr/spip.php?rubrique10&lang=fr|title=Institut Parisien de Chimie Moléculaire - Glycochimie Organique Biologique et Supramoléculaire (GOBS)|website=www.ipcm.fr|accessdate=Apr 24, 2020}}</ref>

== Scientific work ==
Pierre Sinaÿ's scientific work focuses on the chemistry of [[carbohydrate]]s and the understanding of the role of [[oligosaccharide]]s in the living world. In the mid-1970s, Pierre Sinaÿ discovered and developed an effective method for oligosaccharide synthesis known as [[imidate]] [[glycosylation]].<ref>J.-R. Pougny, J.-C. Jacquinet, M. Nassr, D. Duchet, M.-L. Milat, P. Sinaÿ, « A novel synthesis of 1,2 cis-disaccharides », ''Journal of the American Chemical Society'', 1977, 99, <abbr>p.</abbr> 6762-63</ref> This, by now allowing access to increasingly complex carbohydrate structures, is not unrelated to the development of [[glycobiology]], the aim of which is to decode the meaning of this third alphabet of saccharides, which is in addition to that of [[protein]]s and [[nucleic acid]]s. He synthesized the [[antigen]]ic determinants of substances in [[Human Blood groups|human blood groups]]<ref>J.-C. Jacquinet, D. Duchet, M.-L. Milat, P. Sinaÿ, « Synthesis of blood group substances », ''Journal of the Chemical Society, Perkin Transactions'', 1, 1981, <abbr>p.</abbr> 186-91</ref> and then synthesized a complexly structured pentasaccharide representing the active site of [[heparin]] responsible for its [[antithrombotic]] effect.<ref>J. Choay, M. Petitou, J.-C. Lormeau, P. Sinaÿ, B. Casu, G. Gatti, « Structure-activity relationship in heparin : a synthetic pentasaccharide with high affinity for antithrombin III and eliciting high anti-factor Xa activity », ''Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications'', 1983, 116, <abbr>p.</abbr> 492</ref> This last achievement demonstrates for the first time, without any ambiguity, the molecular basis of such an activity, commonly used in hospital medicine. This breakthrough in glyco-chemistry has led to the concept of conformational flexibility,<ref>B. Casu, J. Choay, D.R. Ferro, G. Gatti, J.-C. Jacquinet, M. Petitou, A. Provasoli, M. Ragazzi, P. Sinaÿ, G. Torri, « Controversial glycosaminoglycan conformations », ''Nature'', 1986, 322, <abbr>p.</abbr> 215-16</ref><ref>B. Casu, M. Petitou, M. Provasoli, P. Sinaÿ, « Conformational flexibility : a new concept for explaining binding and biological properties of iduronic acid-containing glycosaminoglycans », ''Trends in Biochemical Sciences'', 1988, 13, <abbr>p.</abbr> 221-25</ref> which is crucial in heparinology. First materialized by the use of [[nuclear magnetic resonance]],<ref>D.R. Ferro, A. Provasoli, M. Ragazzi, G. Torri, B. Casu, G. Gatti, J.-C. Jacquinet, P. Sinaÿ, M. Petitou, J. Choay, « Evidence for conformational equilibrium of the sulfated L-iduronate residue in heparin and in synthetic heparin mono- and oligo-saccharides : NMR and force-field studies », ''Journal of the American Chemical Society'', 1986, 108, <abbr>p.</abbr> 6773-78</ref> this concept was studied in detail using the chemical synthesis of constrained sugars adopting unconventional conformations.<ref>S.K. Das, J.-C. Mallet, J. Esnault, P.-A. Driguez, P. Duchaussoy, P. Sizun, J.-P. Herault, J.-M. Herbert, M. Petitou, P. Sinaÿ, « Synthesis of conformationally locked L- iduronic acid derivatives : direct evidence for a critical role of the skew-boat 2S0 conformer in the activation of antithrombin by heparin », ''Chemistry- A European Journal'', 2001, 7, <abbr>p.</abbr> 4821-34</ref> Pierre Sinaÿ has also discovered and developed a whole series of conceptually new reactions. Selective examples include the synthesis of spiroorthoesters by using [[selenium]] chemistry,<ref>G. Jaurand, J.-M. Beau, P. Sinaÿ, « Organoselenium chemistry : stereoselective conversion of glycals into anomeric spiroorthoesters using a glycosyloxyselenation- oxidation elimination sequence », ''Journal of the Chemical Society, Chemical Communications'', 1982, 12, <abbr>p.</abbr> 1701-03</ref> the development of organometallic chemistry of [[anomer]]ic carbon,<ref>J.-M. Lancelin, L. Morin-Allory, P. Sinaÿ,, « Simple generation of a reactive glycosyl-lithium derivative », ''Journal of the Chemical Society, Chemical Communications'', 1984, 6, <abbr>p.</abbr> 355-56</ref><ref>P. de Pouilly, A. Chenede, J.-M. Mallet, P. Sinaÿ, « Samarium diiodide-promoted chemistry at the anomeric center of carbohydrates. Reductive formation and reaction of samarium (III) reagents », ''Bulletin de la Société Chimique de France'', 1993, 130, <abbr>p.</abbr> 256-65</ref> the pioneering synthesis of C-disaccharides,<ref>V. C. Xin, J.-M. Mallet, P. Sinaÿ, « An expeditious synthesis of C-disaccharide using a temporary silaketal connection », ''Journal of the Chemical Society, Chemical Communications'', 1993, 10, <abbr>p.</abbr> 864</ref> electrochemical glycosylation<ref>C. Amatore, A. Jutand, J.-M. Mallet, G. Meyer, P. Sinaÿ, « Electrochemical glycosylation using phenyl S-glycosides », ''Journal of the Chemical Society, Chemical Communications'', 1990, 9, <abbr>p.</abbr> 718</ref> and, more recently, a novel functionalization of cyclodextrins through a kind of molecular [[microsurgery]] in which [[aluminium]] derivatives are said to be the scalpel.<ref>A. J. Pearce, P. Sinaÿ, « Diisobutylaluminum-promoted regioselective de-O-benzylation of perbenzylated cyclodextrins : a powerful new strategy for the preparation of selectively modified cyclodextrins », ''Angewandte Chemie, International Edition'', 2000, 39, <abbr>p.</abbr> 3610-12</ref> For the first time, the existence of the glycosyl [[Ion|cation]], an intermediate conventionally postulated during glycosylation reactions, could be formally demonstrated through chemistry in a superacid environment.<ref>A. Martin, A. Arda, J. Désiré, A. Martin- Mingot, N. Probst, P. Sinaÿ J. Jimenez-Barbero, S. Thibaudeau, Y. Blériot, « Catching elusive glycosyl cations in a condensed phase with HF/SbF5- superacid », ''Nature Chemistry'', 2016, 8</ref> A 4-volume book covers many aspects of carbohydrate chemistry and biology.<ref>B. Ernst, G. W. Hart, P. Sinaÿ, Carbohydrates in Chemistry and Biology, ouvrage en 4 volumes, Wiley-VCH, 2000 ({{ISBN|3-527-29511-9}})</ref>

== Awards and honours ==

* &nbsp;&nbsp; Achille Le Bel Grand Prize of the [[Société chimique de France|French Chemical Society]] (1979)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.societechimiquedefrance.fr/fr/achille-le-bel.html|title=Lauréats du Grand Prix Achille Le Bel|accessdate=Apr 24, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100216231405/http://www.societechimiquedefrance.fr/fr/achille-le-bel.html|archive-date=February 16, 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* &nbsp;&nbsp; Pierre Desnuelle Prize from the French Academy of sciences (1996)
* &nbsp;&nbsp; Medal of the [[Berthelot Foundation]] (1996)
* &nbsp;&nbsp; Claude S. Hudson Award in Carbohydrate Chemistry from the [[American Chemical Society]] (2007)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en.html|title=American Chemical Society|website=American Chemical Society|accessdate=Apr 24, 2020}}</ref>
* &nbsp;&nbsp; Elected Correspondent of the [[French Academy of Sciences|French Academy of sciences]] (1996)<ref name="academie" />
* &nbsp;&nbsp; Honorary doctorate from the [[University of Lisbon]] (2005)
* &nbsp;&nbsp; Elected member of the French Academy of sciences (2003)<ref name="academie" />
* &nbsp;&nbsp; Haworth Memorial Reading and Haworth Medal from the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (Great Britain, 2011).
* &nbsp;&nbsp; Associate Member of the [[National Academy of Pharmacy]] (2016).<ref>{{cite web|title=Académie nationale de Pharmacie|url=https://www.acadpharm.org/qui_sommes_nous/aff_membre.php?memb_id=1308&fil_post=CAT-MEA&fil_nom=sinay&fil_sect=&que_act=O&fil_pays=&fil_bureau=&fil_conseil=&page=&ipp=|publication-date=}}</ref>
* &nbsp;&nbsp; Chevalier of the [[Légion d’Honneur|Légion d'honneur]] and Commandeur of the [[Ordre des Palmes académiques|Palmes Académiques]].
